title: Brightwater Energy starts a 100-hour iron-air battery pilot
body: Brightwater Energy switched on an iron-air battery in Oakridge that can discharge for up to 100 hours [1]. The 10-megawatt pilot will run for two years before the utility decides on a larger order [1][2].
why_it_matters: Batteries that last days rather than hours could let grids rely on wind and solar through calm weeks [2].

title: Kelso Cement captures carbon at its Dunmore kiln
body: Kelso Cement began capturing carbon dioxide from the kiln at its Dunmore plant, aiming for 400,000 tonnes a year [1]. The gas will be piped to a depleted offshore gas field for storage [2].
why_it_matters: Cement kilns release carbon dioxide from the limestone itself, which cleaner fuel alone cannot remove [1].

title: Regulators approve Northwind Grid's 2-gigawatt offshore wind link
body: Regulators approved Northwind Grid's undersea cable linking two offshore wind farms to the mainland [1]. Construction starts next spring and the link should carry 2 gigawatts by 2030 [1].
why_it_matters: Wind farms far from shore need cables like this one to bring their power to cities [2].

title: Solace cuts the price of its heat pump by 18 percent
body: Solace lowered the price of its home heat pump by 18 percent after moving production to a new factory [1]. The company says installation now takes one day instead of three [2].
why_it_matters: Upfront cost is the main reason households give for keeping gas boilers [2].

title: Verdant Fuels opens a solar-powered hydrogen plant in Port Ellis
body: Verdant Fuels opened a 50-megawatt electrolyser in Port Ellis that splits water with power from a nearby solar farm [1]. Its first customer is a fertiliser maker that will stop using hydrogen made from gas [1][2].
why_it_matters: Fertiliser and steel makers need hydrogen, and making it without gas removes a large industrial source of emissions [2].

title: Halden Ridge Observatory finds a comet bound for the inner solar system
body: Astronomers at Halden Ridge Observatory found a comet that will pass inside the orbit of Mars next March [1]. It may be visible through binoculars for about three weeks around its closest approach [2].
why_it_matters: Comets from the outer solar system carry ice that has changed little since the planets formed [1].

title: Aurora Launch Systems lands its booster on a sea platform
body: Aurora Launch Systems landed the first stage of its Kestrel rocket on a floating platform after launching a weather satellite [1]. The company plans to fly the same booster again within 60 days [2].
why_it_matters: Reusing boosters is the main way launch companies cut the cost of reaching orbit [2].

title: The Lumen lunar lander loses contact before touchdown
body: Mission controllers lost contact with the Lumen lander about two kilometres above the Moon's surface [1]. The team is studying the last telemetry and has not said whether the lander crashed [2].
why_it_matters: Lumen was to test drilling for ice near the lunar south pole, a resource future crews could use for water and fuel [1].

title: The Corvid space telescope releases its first deep-field image
body: The Corvid telescope released its first deep-field image, showing about 4,000 galaxies in a patch of sky smaller than a grain of rice held at arm's length [1]. Some appear as they were less than a billion years after the Big Bang [2].
why_it_matters: Deep fields show how the first galaxies grew, which models of the early universe must explain [2].

title: Tessera station crew stays two more weeks after a capsule leak
body: The three-person crew of the Tessera station will stay two extra weeks while engineers study a small coolant leak on their return capsule [1]. Mission managers say the crew is safe and supplies last until December [2].
why_it_matters: A capsule that cannot be trusted for the trip home is the most serious problem a station crew can face [2].

title: Hollis Bank confirms a breach of 1.2 million customer records
body: Hollis Bank said attackers copied the names, addresses and account numbers of 1.2 million customers from a marketing system run by a supplier [1]. The bank says no passwords or card numbers were taken [1].
why_it_matters: Stolen account details make phishing messages that pretend to come from the bank more convincing [2].

title: A flaw in Quillmail let users read other people's inboxes
body: Researchers found a flaw in the Quillmail webmail server that let any logged-in user read other users' messages [1]. A patch is available and administrators are urged to install it this week [2].
why_it_matters: Quillmail runs the email of many small organisations that have no security staff of their own [2].

title: Ransomware shuts Medvale Hospital's appointment system
body: A ransomware attack forced Medvale Hospital to cancel non-urgent appointments for five days [1]. Emergency care continued on paper records while the systems were restored from backups [2].
why_it_matters: Hospitals are frequent ransomware targets because downtime puts pressure on them to pay quickly [2].

title: Police take down the Grindstone botnet
body: Police in four countries seized the servers behind the Grindstone botnet, which had infected about 300,000 home routers [1]. Owners are advised to restart their routers and install the latest firmware [2].
why_it_matters: Infected routers were used to hide attacks and send spam from ordinary home connections [1].

title: Pebble Cloud makes passkeys the default sign-in
body: Pebble Cloud made passkeys the default way to sign in for new accounts and will phase out text-message codes by June [1]. The company says a passkey cannot be phished because it only works on the real site [2].
why_it_matters: Codes sent by text message can be intercepted, which passkeys avoid [2].

title: Vireo Motors recalls 38,000 cars over a charging port fault
body: Vireo Motors is recalling 38,000 Vireo S hatchbacks because the charging port can overheat during fast charging [1]. Owners are asked to charge only at home until a free repair is done [2].
why_it_matters: It is the largest recall of an electric car in the region this year [2].

title: Arclight opens 400 fast chargers along the northern motorway
body: Arclight opened 400 fast chargers at 50 service stations along the northern motorway [1]. Each charger can add about 200 kilometres of range in 15 minutes [2].
why_it_matters: Gaps in motorway charging are a common reason drivers give for not buying an electric car [2].

title: Tamberlane's sodium-ion cells pass 10,000 cycles in lab tests
body: Tamberlane said its sodium-ion cells kept 80 percent of their capacity after 10,000 charging cycles in laboratory tests [1]. The company plans a pilot production line next year [2].
why_it_matters: Sodium is cheaper and more plentiful than lithium, so such cells could make small cars cheaper [2].

title: Carrow retires its last diesel bus
body: The city of Carrow retired its last diesel bus and now runs 220 electric buses on all routes [1]. The transport authority says fuel and maintenance costs fell by a third [2].
why_it_matters: City buses run fixed routes and return to a depot each night, which makes them easy to electrify [2].

title: Vireo Motors cuts the price of its long-range sedan
body: Vireo Motors cut the price of its long-range Vireo L sedan by 4,000 euros [1]. Analysts link the cut to slower sales and new competitors [2].
why_it_matters: Price cuts by one carmaker often push others to follow [2].

title: The Marovian Central Bank holds its rate at 3.25 percent
body: The Marovian Central Bank kept its main interest rate at 3.25 percent for a third meeting in a row [1]. Its governor said inflation is still above the 2 percent target [2].
why_it_matters: Borrowers will wait longer for cheaper mortgages [2].

title: Inflation in Marovia falls to 2.8 percent
body: Consumer prices in Marovia rose 2.8 percent in the year to August, down from 3.4 percent in July [1]. Lower energy prices did most of the work [2].
why_it_matters: Slowing inflation makes a rate cut more likely later in the year [2].

title: The Kessler Exchange halts trading for 40 minutes
body: Trading on the Kessler Exchange stopped for 40 minutes after a software update broke the system that matches buy and sell orders [1]. The exchange said no trades were lost [2].
why_it_matters: Outages at an exchange leave investors unable to buy or sell when prices move [2].

title: Bayview Bank's bond sale draws record demand
body: Bayview Bank sold 2 billion in ten-year bonds after investors placed orders worth 9 billion [1]. The strong demand let the bank pay a lower interest rate than it first offered [2].
why_it_matters: Heavy demand for bank bonds suggests investors see little risk in the banking sector [2].

title: The Marovian Central Bank starts a digital currency trial
body: The Marovian Central Bank started a six-month trial of a digital currency with 5,000 volunteers and 30 shops [1]. The bank says it has not decided whether to issue the currency to everyone [2].
why_it_matters: A digital currency issued by the central bank would compete with bank deposits and card payments [2].

title: The MV-9 malaria vaccine trial in Lanzeri reports 72 percent protection
body: The trial of the MV-9 malaria vaccine in Lanzeri found 72 percent fewer cases among vaccinated children a year after the third dose [1]. The researchers will next test whether a booster keeps protection up [2].
why_it_matters: Malaria remains a leading cause of death in young children in the region [2].

title: Brightgate Hospital tests an AI tool that reads chest X-rays
body: Brightgate Hospital tested an AI tool that flagged 94 percent of the pneumonia cases its radiologists found on chest X-rays [1]. The hospital will use it only to sort scans, with a doctor reading each one [2].
why_it_matters: Sorting scans by urgency could shorten waits for the sickest patients [2].

title: Orrin University grows kidney organoids that filter blood
body: Researchers at Orrin University grew kidney organoids that filtered blood for 48 hours in the laboratory [1]. They say a transplantable organ is still many years away [2].
why_it_matters: Lab-grown kidney tissue could one day be used to test drugs for kidney damage [2].

title: The antibiotic solvamycin clears a resistant infection in mice
body: A new antibiotic, solvamycin, cleared a drug-resistant bacterial infection in mice within four days [1]. Human trials could start in two years if safety tests go well [2].
why_it_matters: Few new classes of antibiotic have reached patients in decades, while resistance keeps spreading [2].

title: The Pellham trial of a weekly insulin ends early
body: The Pellham trial of a once-weekly insulin stopped early because the results were already clear [1]. Blood sugar control matched daily injections with fewer low-sugar episodes [1][2].
why_it_matters: Fewer injections could help people with diabetes keep to their treatment [2].

title: Lantern Forge delays Emberfall to next March
body: Lantern Forge delayed its fantasy game Emberfall from November to next March to fix performance problems on older consoles [1]. Players who pre-ordered can ask for a refund [2].
why_it_matters: Emberfall was the studio's biggest release planned for the holiday season [2].

title: The Pocket Arcade handheld sells 2 million units in a month
body: The Pocket Arcade handheld console sold 2 million units in its first month [1]. Its maker says stock shortages will last until the new year [2].
why_it_matters: Strong handheld sales show players still want dedicated gaming devices [2].

title: Studio Moth's union signs its first contract
body: Developers at Studio Moth signed their first union contract, which includes a trial of a 32-hour working week [1]. The contract also limits overtime in the months before a release [2].
why_it_matters: Long periods of overtime before a release have been a common complaint in the games industry [2].

title: Starfall Online will shut its servers in January
body: Publisher Gyre Interactive will close the servers of Starfall Online on January 15, eight years after launch [1]. Players will keep an offline mode with the story missions [2].
why_it_matters: Online-only games can become unplayable when their servers close [2].

title: Emberfall's open beta draws 300,000 players
body: The open beta of Emberfall drew 300,000 players over its first weekend [1]. Lantern Forge says crash reports from the beta will guide the fixes before launch [2].
why_it_matters: A large beta gives the studio data that internal testing cannot [2].

title: Tamsin Labs releases Kestrel-7 under Apache 2.0
body: Tamsin Labs released Kestrel-7, a 7-billion-parameter language model whose weights anyone can download under the Apache 2.0 license [1]. It runs on a laptop with 16 GB of memory [2].
why_it_matters: A permissive license lets companies build products on the model without paying fees [2].

title: Kestrel-7 tops a coding benchmark for small models
body: Kestrel-7 scored highest among models under 10 billion parameters on a public coding benchmark [1]. Its makers say it was trained on a large set of permissively licensed code [2].
why_it_matters: Small models that code well can run on a developer's own machine instead of a paid service [2].

title: Orrery AI publishes the training data list for its open model
body: Orrery AI published the full list of 1,400 data sources used to train its open-weight model [1]. Researchers can now check which websites and books it learned from [2].
why_it_matters: Few model makers disclose their training data, which makes their models hard to audit [2].

title: Quantised Larkspur-70B runs on a single graphics card
body: Community developers released 4-bit versions of the Larkspur-70B model that run on one consumer graphics card [1]. They report a small drop in answer quality on standard tests [2].
why_it_matters: Running a large model at home keeps data off third-party servers [2].

title: A role-play jailbreak works on five open models
body: Researchers found that a role-play prompt bypassed the safety training of five open-weight models, including Kestrel-7 and Larkspur-70B [1]. They shared it with the developers 60 days before publishing [2].
why_it_matters: Open weights cannot be recalled once downloaded, so safety fixes reach users slowly [2].
